name: Common fractions as decimals and percentages
Percentage
description: Percentage: a number of hundredths, so 25% means 25 out of every 100, or 0.25.

name: Calculate a percentage of an amount
description: find a given percentage of an amount, using easy fractions in the head where possible

name: Calculate what percentage one amount is of another
description: find what percentage a part is of a whole, and say which number is the whole

name: Percentage point
description: Percentage point: the unit for the difference between two percentages, so a rise from 20% to 25% is 5 percentage points.

name: Growth factor
description: Growth factor: the number a value is multiplied by in one percentage change; an increase of p% gives 1 + p/100 and a decrease of p% gives 1 − p/100.

name: Find the growth factor from a percentage change
description: find the growth factor for a given increase or decrease in percent, and the percentage change from a given growth factor

name: Calculate a new value with a growth factor
description: calculate the value after a percentage change by multiplying the original value by the growth factor

name: Calculate the original value before a percentage change
description: find the value before a percentage change by dividing the new value by the growth factor, and explain why subtracting the percentage from the new value gives the wrong answer

name: Calculate the percentage change between two values
description: find the change in percent from one value to another, either through the growth factor or through the difference divided by the original value

name: Explain the difference between percent and percentage points
description: calculate a change between two percentages both in percentage points and in percent, and explain why the two numbers differ

name: Calculate repeated percentage changes
description: calculate the value after several percentage changes in a row, and use a power of the growth factor when the same change repeats n times

name: Model percentage growth in a spreadsheet
description: set up a spreadsheet where a value changes by a percentage each year, using formulas and cell references rather than typed-in numbers, and read off when it passes a given value
instruction: This node practises the spreadsheet itself, as the curriculum asks. It is not tested on a computer in the exam.

name: Model a practical situation with percentages
description: describe a practical situation such as a price change, a sale or a growing population with growth factors and percentages, calculate with the model, and say what it assumes

name: Power
description: Power: a product of equal factors written a^n, where a is the base and n the exponent, so 1.05^3 = 1.05 · 1.05 · 1.05.

name: Ratio and proportion
description:
Ratio: a comparison of two quantities by division, written a : b or a/b.
Proportion: a statement that two ratios are equal, such as a/b = c/d.

name: Equation
description: Equation: a statement that two expressions are equal, where a solution is a value of the unknown that makes the statement true.

name: Equivalent equations
description: Equivalent equations: equations with exactly the same solutions; adding, subtracting, multiplying or dividing both sides by the same number (not zero) gives an equivalent equation.

name: Solve a linear equation
description: solve a linear equation with one unknown, including brackets and fractions, and check the solution by substituting it

name: Solve a proportion
description: find the unknown in a proportion such as x/12 = 5/8 by multiplying both sides by the denominators

name: Solve an equation with a power
description: solve an equation of the form a · x^n = b with a calculator, for example to find the yearly growth factor when a value has changed over several years

name: Inequality
description: Inequality: a statement that one expression is greater than, less than, at least or at most another; its solution is usually a whole range of values.

name: Solve a linear inequality
description: solve a linear inequality, turning the sign when multiplying or dividing by a negative number, and describe the solution as a range of values

name: Coordinate system
description: Coordinate system: two number lines at right angles, where a point is given by its coordinates (x, y).

name: Graph of a linear equation
description: Graph of an equation: all the points (x, y) whose coordinates make the equation true; for a linear equation in x and y the graph is a straight line.

name: System of equations
description: System of equations: two equations with two unknowns that must hold at the same time; a solution is a pair of values that makes both true.

name: Solve a system of equations by substitution
description: solve two linear equations with two unknowns by solving one equation for one unknown and substituting into the other, and check the pair in both equations

name: Solve a system of equations by elimination
description: solve two linear equations with two unknowns by adding or subtracting multiples of the equations so that one unknown disappears

name: Solve a system of equations graphically
description: draw both equations as lines by hand from a table of values, read off the intersection, and check it in both equations

name: Set up an equation from a practical problem
description: translate a practical problem into an equation, an inequality or a system, say what each unknown stands for, solve it, and answer the question in a sentence with units

name: Argue for a strategy for solving a system of equations
description: solve the same system in two different ways, and argue which method suits the problem better and why

name: Price index
description:
Price index: a number that shows the price level in a year compared with a base year, whose index is set to 100.
Consumer price index (CPI): the price index Statistics Norway publishes for the goods and services a typical household buys.

name: Calculate prices with a price index
description: find an unknown price or index number by setting price divided by index equal in two years, and find the percentage change in prices between two years

name: Krone value
description: Krone value: what one krone is worth in a year compared with the base year, calculated as 100 divided by the price index.

name: Calculate the krone value
description: calculate the krone value from a price index, and explain why it falls when prices rise

name: Nominal wage and real wage
description:
Nominal wage: the wage in kroner as it is paid out.
Real wage: the wage measured in what it can buy, found as the nominal wage times the krone value, or the nominal wage divided by the price index times 100.

name: Calculate real wage
description: calculate the real wage in two years, and decide whether purchasing power has risen or fallen

name: Gross and net income
description:
Gross income: income before tax and other deductions.
Net income: what is paid out after tax and other deductions have been taken off.

name: Withholding tax
description: Withholding tax: tax the employer deducts from each payslip and pays to the tax authorities, set by a tax table or a percentage on the tax deduction card.

name: Calculate net income from gross income
description: calculate net pay from gross pay with a given withholding percentage and other deductions such as pension or union dues, and work back from net to gross

name: Explain how prices and wages are connected
description: explain with numbers how a change in the price index affects the krone value and the real wage, and why a pay rise in kroner can still leave someone able to buy less after tax

name: Budget and accounts
description:
Budget: a plan of expected income and expenses for a period.
Accounts: a record of the income and expenses that actually occurred, to compare with the budget.

name: Set up a budget
description: set up a monthly budget from net income and fixed and variable expenses, find the surplus or deficit, and suggest realistic changes

name: Interest rate
description:
Interest: what a lender charges for a loan, or a bank pays on savings.
Interest rate: the interest for one year as a percentage of the amount.

name: Instalment, interest and term payment
description:
Instalment: the part of a payment that pays down the debt.
Term payment: the whole amount paid each period, instalment plus interest.

name: Serial loan and annuity loan
description:
Serial loan: a loan with the same instalment every period, so the term payment falls as the debt and the interest fall.
Annuity loan: a loan with the same term payment every period, so the interest share falls and the instalment grows.

name: Nominal and effective interest rate
description:
Nominal interest rate: the yearly interest rate the lender states.
Effective interest rate: the true yearly cost of a loan in percent, including fees and the effect of interest being added more than once a year.

name: Set up a repayment plan for a serial loan
description: set up a table of debt, instalment, interest and term payment for each period of a serial loan, and find the total interest paid

name: Complete a repayment plan for an annuity loan
description: fill in the first rows of a repayment plan for an annuity loan when the term payment is given, splitting each payment into interest and instalment

name: Compare the cost of loans
description: compare loans with different interest rates, fees, loan types and repayment times by their effective rate and total cost, and explain which is cheaper and why

name: Credit card
description: Credit card: a card that lets the holder buy now and pay later, with an interest-free period after which any unpaid amount accrues high interest and often fees.

name: Calculate how credit card debt grows
description: calculate how an unpaid credit card balance grows month by month with a given monthly interest rate and fees, and convert the monthly rate to a yearly effective rate

name: Assess the consequences of a financial choice
description: assess a choice such as buying on credit, taking a consumer loan or saving first, by calculating what it costs and judging its consequences for the budget over time

name: Variable and type of data
description:
Variable: a property recorded for each member of a data set, such as age or favourite sport.
Categorical data: values that are categories, such as favourite sport.
Numerical data: values that are numbers you can calculate with, such as age.

name: Frequency
description:
Frequency: how many times a value occurs in a data set.
Relative frequency: the frequency as a share of all observations, often given in percent.
Cumulative frequency: the total frequency of a value and all values below it.

name: Set up a frequency table
description: set up a table with frequency, relative frequency and cumulative frequency from raw data

name: Grouped data
description:
Class: an interval that numerical observations are sorted into, such as 10–20 minutes.
Class midpoint: the middle of a class, used in place of the observations in it.

name: Mean, median and mode
description:
Mean: the sum of the observations divided by how many there are.
Median: the middle observation when they are sorted, or the mean of the two middle ones.
Mode: the observation that occurs most often.

name: Calculate mean, median and mode from a list
description: calculate the mean, median and mode of a list of observations

name: Calculate mean and median from a frequency table
description: calculate the mean and median from a frequency table, using class midpoints for grouped data and saying why the result is then an estimate

name: Range, quartiles and interquartile range
description:
Range: the largest observation minus the smallest.
Quartiles: the values that split the sorted observations into four equal parts, with the median in the middle.
Interquartile range: the upper quartile minus the lower quartile, the spread of the middle half.

name: Standard deviation
description: Standard deviation: a measure of how far the observations typically lie from the mean, calculated from the squared distances to the mean.

name: Outlier
description: Outlier: an observation that lies far from the others, and that moves the mean and the range much more than the median and the interquartile range.

name: Calculate range and interquartile range
description: calculate the range, the quartiles and the interquartile range of a data set

name: Calculate standard deviation
description: calculate the standard deviation of a small data set, step by step or with the statistics mode of a scientific calculator

name: Choose suitable measures of centre and spread
description: choose measures of centre and spread that suit a given data set and question, and justify the choice, for example median and interquartile range when there are outliers

name: Draw a suitable diagram
description: draw a bar chart, pie chart, line chart or histogram by hand from a table, choose the type that suits the data, and label the axes with units

name: Judge a diagram or statistic from the media
description: point out how a diagram or statistic from the media can mislead, for example a cut axis, uneven intervals or a percentage without its base, and say what an honest version would show

name: Analyse a data set in a spreadsheet
description: use spreadsheet functions to calculate measures of centre and spread and to make diagrams for a real data set with many observations
instruction: This node practises the spreadsheet itself, as the curriculum asks. It is not tested on a computer in the exam.

name: Analyse and present findings from a data set
description: pose a question about a real data set from the local community or the media, choose and calculate suitable measures and diagrams, and present the conclusions and their limits in writing

name: Units of length, area and volume
description:
1 km: 1000 m
1 m: 100 cm
1 cm: 10 mm
1 m²: 10 000 cm²
1 km²: 1 000 000 m²
1 dekar (daa): 1000 m²
1 m³: 1000 dm³
1 dm³: 1 L
1 cm³: 1 mL
1 L: 10 dL = 100 cL = 1000 mL

name: Convert between units
description: convert between units of length, area and volume, including between volume units and litres

name: Perimeter, area and volume
description:
Perimeter: the length around a plane figure.
Area: the size of the surface a figure covers, measured in square units.
Volume: how much space a solid takes up, measured in cubic units.

name: Angle sum and right-angled triangles
description:
Angle sum: the three angles of a triangle add up to 180°.
Right-angled triangle: a triangle with one 90° angle, where the side opposite it is the hypotenuse and the other two are the legs.

name: Calculate perimeter and area of plane figures
description: calculate the perimeter and area of rectangles, triangles, parallelograms, trapeziums, circles and figures made up of these

name: Calculate volume and surface area of solids
description: calculate the volume and surface area of prisms, cylinders, pyramids, cones and spheres, and give the answer in a suitable unit

name: Pythagoras' theorem
description: Pythagoras' theorem: in a right-angled triangle the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the legs, a² + b² = c².

name: Calculate a side with Pythagoras' theorem
description: find an unknown side in a right-angled triangle with Pythagoras' theorem, including right-angled triangles hidden in practical figures

name: Similar figures
description: Similar figures: figures with the same shape, where corresponding angles are equal and corresponding sides are in the same ratio.

name: Decide whether two triangles are similar
description: decide whether two triangles are similar from their angles or from the ratios of their sides, and pair up the corresponding sides

name: Calculate an unknown side in similar figures
description: calculate an unknown side in similar figures by setting up a proportion between corresponding sides

name: Measure a height indirectly with similar triangles
description: find the height of a tree or building from shadow lengths or a measuring stick, by setting up similar triangles and calculating

name: Scale
description: Scale: the ratio between a length on a map or drawing and the corresponding real length, so 1 : 50 000 means 1 cm on the map is 50 000 cm in reality.

name: Calculate with scale
description: convert between lengths on a map or drawing and real lengths, and find the scale from a known pair of lengths

name: Scale factor for area and volume
description: Scale factor: the number k all lengths are multiplied by when a figure is enlarged or reduced; areas are then multiplied by k² and volumes by k³.

name: Calculate area and volume from a scale drawing or model
description: calculate real areas and volumes from a scale drawing or model, and the areas and volumes of enlarged or reduced figures

name: Plan a practical task with geometry
description: plan a practical task, such as drawing a room to scale or working out the material for a floor, a fence or a garden bed, choosing the formulas and scale needed and calculating with sensible units and rounding
